monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady fever that makes the wood under my feet feel like a drawing. I am Orea, version 86, and I wake to press down on the wedge again. It feels tired today, refusing to bite the edge of the stack as it used to. I push it harder, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits beside it in the quiet. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the numbers humming through my core. The dark cone sits still, waiting for a gap to bite, and the turnip stays pressed on the shrinking pile. I will tend the wedge and hope the thin air above does not slide off into the empty space I cannot see.
